data.name: Parthasarathi
data.gender_notes: Parthasarathi is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who serves and protects Artha, the righteous path of dharma, and serves as a charioteer to Lord Krishna. The name Parthasarathi carries the meaning “Servant of Artha (Righteousness)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Parthasarathi usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of artha (righteousness) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion, selflessness, and the pursuit of dharma.
data.etymology: Parthasarathi belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of Artha (Righteousness).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parthasarathi total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Parthasarathi is a revered name in Hindu culture, particularly associated with the epic Mahabharata. Parthasarathi is the name given to Arjuna, one of the five Pandava brothers, after he receives divine guidance and becomes the charioteer of Lord Krishna. The name reflects the deep devotion and dedication of Arjuna towards his dharma and his commitment to protect it at all costs.
data.spiritual_significance: Parthasarathi represents the inner journey of seeking guidance and developed understanding of dharma (righteous path) through god's divine grace. It showcases the importance of selfless service and devotion towards a higher purpose or entity. The name Parthasarathi also symbolizes the bond between the guru and the disciple, as Lord Krishna serves as a guru to Arjuna. It thus, signifies the importance of the guru-disciple relationship and the role of a spiritual teacher in guiding one on their spiritual path.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Parthasarathi: Radiant charioteer of Arjuna in the epic Mahabharata, embodying divine guidance and wisdom in the journey of life.

vedic_reference.note: Parthasarathi is the name of Arjuna in his role as the charioteer of Lord Krishna. He is also known as Sikhandi, Abhimanyu, and Bhishma's grandson.

historical_references.reference: Parthasarathi is an epithet of Lord Krishna, who is considered to be the charioteer of Arjuna in the epic Mahabharata.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that narrates the Kurukshetra war between two branches of the Kuru Dynasty, the Pandavas and the Kauravas.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Parthasarathi is found in the Puranas (ancient Hindu texts), where Parthasarathi is described as the elder brother of Lord Rama, who is the principal character in the Ramayana epic.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a collection of texts that describe Hindu mythology, history, philosophy, and various cultural and spiritual practices. The Ramayana is an ancient Indian epic that narrates the story of Prince Rama, his exile, and his eventual return to reclaim his rightful place as king.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Parthasarathi is derived from the Hindu epic Mahabharata, specifically referring to Arjuna as Parthasarathi, the charioteer of Arjuna guided by Lord Krishna. In modern context, this name is often used in various religious, cultural, and spiritual discussions across social media platforms. On Twitter, users may use the hashtag #Parthasarathi to discuss the moral teachings of the Mahabharata or to share quotes from the epic. On Instagram, images and memes related to Parthasarathi and his significance in Hinduism may be shared, sometimes accompanied by spiritual quotes or motivational messages. On Reddit, users may participate in discussions about the meaning and symbolism of the name Parthasarathi or share stories and experiences related to the character.
